messages:
marco: quick alert
After the 'prefetch-scan' kernel heuristic landed p95 host-side for very short chats jumped ~35ms. GPU timelines look identical.

marco: sample from trace agent (short-chat):
```
host_total_ms p50: 1.1  p95: 92 (+35)  p99: 130
parse_tokenize_ms p95: 21.7 (+18)
hpack_decode_ms p95: 8.3 (new hotspot)
stream_writev_calls p95: 3 (was 1)
kvcache_lookup_ms p95: 1.2
```

sana: HPACK decode? That's interesting. Prefetch-scan peeks into the HTTP/2 header block to fingerprint. If the peek forces a full HPACK decode on the hot path that would explain both CPU and alloc spikes.

yves: Yes, the new scanner calls header_decoder.decode_frame() to extract pseudo-headers for fingerprinting. That API lazily triggers dynamic table updates and can allocate+memcpy. On small requests it's dominating time.

marco: Flamegraph shows hpack.decode -> dynamic_table_update -> memmove -> utf8_normalize -> token_adapter_legacy. The token routing then loads ICU in some cases. Also saw many small TLS record writes causing writev split at the transport.

sana: Repro: run grpc short prompt with metadata A=1 -> slow trace shows open("/usr/lib/icu/...") and repeated writev syscalls. Strace showed hpack decoder doing multiple reads and allocations on the slow run.

yves: Blamelist: c3f9b1 (prefetch-scan) -> d2a8ff (transport chunk-align tweak). Both landed within the same window. The fingerprint peek used to only inspect raw bytes; now we signed off on decoded header keys which triggered HPACK work.

marco: Ops-bot rolled back c3f9b1 on canary at 09:05 UTC.

ops-bot: rollback: reverted c3f9b1 on eng-runtime/canary at 09:05 UTC.

marco: After rollback p95 returned close to baseline in ~6m. KV stats steady. Root cause confirmed: inline HPACK decode + token routing -> legacy adapter.

sana: Proposed fixes:
- avoid full HPACK decode in ingress hot path; use a header-quick-peek that scans compressed header bytes for distinguishing tokens without updating dynamic table
- default ambiguous fingerprints to token_adapter_v4 (safe-fast path) rather than legacy
- move any kernel-blob mmap/prefetch off the request CPU path (make prefetch async best-effort)
- restore transport coalescing: only split TLS records when payload > threshold; prefer single writev for short chats
- ascii-only fastpath before any ICU normalization
- add a small e2e perf test that emits many 1-10 token grpc streams and asserts host p95 < 55ms

yves: I'll send a PR that replaces decode_frame() with a peek_decoder which reads only name bytes (no dynamic table ops) and returns a lightweight hash. Also change safe-default mapping.

marco: I'll work transport coalesce + ensure chunk-align won't break writev semantics. Sana can add ascii-fastpath and perf test.

ops-bot: scheduling stateless-canary with prefetch disabled and transport-coalesce enabled at 09:40 UTC; collecting traces for 20m.

sana: Also add telemetry to expose how many requests route to legacy vs v4 adapter so we can detect regressions early.

marco: Good call. Marking incident P1 for Hosted and P0 for Dedicated until we ship the lightweight peek + coalesce patch. Paste traces in-thread. :thumbsup:
